ftest.spm_test_version: Julias 30 questions + Foundation Sample Paper Feb15

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following Agile approaches deals with projects and not just the development and delivery of a product?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 2.5 - The other three approaches are seen as lightweight, with minimum structure and guidance, DSDM focusses on the wider business need and on all aspects of the solution that evolves to meet that need.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following is not a description of an agile style of working?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 2.3 - DSDM advocates that projects should do enough design up front to allow the project to move to the next step.

spm_options.spm_option: Working closely with the customer throughout
Ensuring the final solution actually meets the business need
Making decisions about the detail as soon as possible

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following statements about DSDM are true? 1. May be used to supplement an existing in-house Agile approach. 2. Deals with the development and delivery of a product rather than the full project. 3. Works alongside existing standards and approaches. 4. Suited to the development of new solutions and enhancing existing solutions

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 2.5 - DSDM has a broader focus than most Agile approaches in that it deals with projects rather than just the development and delivery of a product.

spm_questions.spm_question: According to DSDM philosophy is that any project must be aligned to clearly defined [?] goals

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.1 - DSDM philosophy states that "best business value emerges when projects are aligned to clear business goals, deliver frequently and involve the collaboration of motivated and empowered people".

spm_questions.spm_question: Which project parameter is variable in a DSDM approach?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 3.2 - The DSDM approach to project management fixes time, cost and quality while contingency is managed by varying the features to be delivered.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of these statements does NOT justify the eight principles of DSDM?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.0 - The minimum useable subset of requirements are used by the MoSCoW technique, not a principle

spm_options.spm_option: Principles define the highest attitude and mind set by the team
Principles define the minimum useable subset of requirements
Applying all principles ensures maximum benefit

spm_questions.spm_question: At each [] of product development a result is achieved that gets successively closer to the desired outcome.

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.1 - This is a description of Iterative development

spm_questions.spm_question: Which statement relates to the DSDM view on formality and scalability?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.9 - Typically this is achieved by configuring a lifecycle appropriate for a specific project and determining an appropriate level of formality with which the DSDM products are defined, created and approved.

spm_options.spm_option: The aim is to remove all formality, so that the team can get on with building the solution
Agile must be informal, otherwise it stops being fun
It is entirely formal, to enable management and control
The DSDM process can be configured and calibrated to cater for a range of projects

spm_questions.spm_question: What in DSDM is designed to shape the attitude and mindset of a DSDM team?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.10 - The eight principles help direct and shape the attitude and mindset of a DSDM team. Compromising any of the principles undermines DSDM’s philosophy, as together they deliver a collective value that outweighs their individual benefits.

spm_questions.spm_question: What is Iterative Development?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.3.1 - This describes Iterative development. With each iteration additional features can be designed, developed and tested.

spm_options.spm_option: A design, develop and test cycle which is repeated until there is a fully functional solution
A gated process where development can not begin until the finished design is complete
An early sample, model or release of a product to test a concept or process
The process and activity of planning, organizing, motivating and controlling resources to achieve a specific goal

spm_questions.spm_question: Which approach correctly reflects the use of MoSCoW prioritisation?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 10.3 - The primary focus initially is to create MoSCoW priorities for the project. However, when deciding what to deliver as part of the Project Increment, the next focus will be to agree MoSCoW priorities for that Increment. So, at this point, a requirement may have two priorities: MoSCoW for the project and MoSCoW for the Increment. Finally, when planning a specific Timebox (at the start of each Timebox) the Solution Development Team will allocate a specific priority for the requirements for this Timebox.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which statement about late delivery is correct for DSDM?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.3 - Delivering a solution on time is a very desirable outcome for a project and is quite often the single most important success factor. Late delivery can often undermine the very rationale for a project, especially where market opportunities or legal deadlines are involved.

spm_options.spm_option: Is acceptable provided sufficient warning is given
Can often undermine the very rationale for a project
Is a fact of life and should be expected
Can be really annoying for the Business

spm_questions.spm_question: What DSDM product describes, at a high level, the requirements that the project needs to address and indicates their priority with respect to meeting the objectives of the project and the needs of the business?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.3 - Consideration of requirements begins in Feasibility and a baseline of the PRL describes the scope of the project as at the end of Foundations.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following is the name of a DSDM principle?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.2 - There are eight principles: Focus on the business need; Deliver on time; Collaborate; Never compromise quality; Build incrementally from firm foundations; Develop iteratively; Communicate continuously and clearly; Demonstrate control.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which outcome is related to the DSDM principle of Collaborate?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.4 - Teams that work in a spirit of active cooperation and commitment will always outperform groups of individuals working only in loose association. Collaboration encourages increased understanding, greater speed and shared ownership, which enable teams to perform at a level that exceeds the sum of their parts.

spm_options.spm_option: Team performance exceeds the sum of the parts

spm_questions.spm_question: Which purpose relates to the Foundations phase?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.4 - The Foundations phase establishes a fundamental understanding of the business rationale for the project, the potential solution and how development and delivery of the solution will be managed.

spm_options.spm_option: Converge over time on an accurate solution that meets a business need
Establish whether the project appears costeffective
Establish how development and delivery of the solution will be managed
Bring a baseline of the solution into operational use

spm_questions.spm_question: Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence: A DSDM project will always deliver a viable solution, as long as the practices of [?] and Timeboxing are followed.

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 3.2 - Delivery of a Minimum SubseT (MUST) of requirements is guaranteed as a worst case scenario.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following statements about building quality using the DSDM process is true? 1. A high-level assessment of the risks to achieving the level of quality required is done during Foundations. 2. Final end-to-end testing during Deployment allows for the testing of back-out procedures.

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 9.6 - (2) The statement is true. Final end-to-end testing, including the testing of back-out procedures, is carried out during Deployment.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which statement is part of the definition of the DSDM Principle 8 – Demonstrate Control?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.9 - This is the DSDM definition of Principle 8 – Demonstrate Control.

spm_options.spm_option: Late delivery can undermine the very rationale for a project
It is vital to ensure transparency of all work being performed by the team
Collaboration encourages increased understanding, greater speed and shared ownership.
It is important to recognize that projects operate within a changing world

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is NOT a DSDM role?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7 - A Team Manager is not role defined in the DSDM approach

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is not one of the three role categories defined in the DSDM approach?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.2.2 - Board is not one of the three role categories.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which role is responsible for the project during its duration?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.4 - This responsibility includes both business and technical delivery aspects of the project from Foundations (if not Feasibility) through to deployment.

spm_questions.spm_question: A Business Sponsor...

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.1 - The Business Sponsor is responsible for the business case throughout the project.

spm_options.spm_option: ..manages business involvement within the solution Development Teams
..communicates and promotes the business vision to the project
..owns the business case for the project

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of these roles is not part of the Solution development team?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.2.2.1 - The Technical Co-ordinator is a Project level role

spm_questions.spm_question: Which role is defined within the Supporting Roles category?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.12 - The Workshop Facilitator is responsible for planning, organising and facilitating workshops.

spm_questions.spm_question: Incremental delivery enables...

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 5.5- An organisation amenable to incremental delivery of solutions into live use will benefit from early return on investment

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is a responsibility of the Project Manager?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.4 - The Project Manger needs to manage the working environment in which the solution is evolving, coordinating all aspects of management of the project at a high level. They leave the detailed planning and actual delivery of the product(s) to the Solution Development Team.

spm_options.spm_option: Defining exactly what the team need to do to deliver the products
Protecting the products from change in order to prevent time and cost overruns
Renegotiate the end date of the project if problems arise within a Timebox

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following is NOT stated as a benefit of using DSDM?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 2.6 - Whilst DSDM’s approach and style is founded on an underlying ethos of common sense, it does not negate the need for training. This is not stated as a benefit.

spm_options.spm_option: The business is more likely to feel ownership of the solution as it evolves
Deployment is more likely to go smoothly, due to the cooperation of all parties
The risk of building the wrong solution is greatly reduced

spm_questions.spm_question: Which roles form part of the Solution Development Team?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.2.2.2 - The Solution Development Team roles are Business Ambassador, Solution Developer, Solution Tester, Business Analyst and Team Leader. These roles form the “engine room” of the project.

spm_options.spm_option: Solution Developer, Business Analyst, Technical Coordinator
Solution Developer, Business Analyst, Business Ambassador
Technical Coordinator, Business Visionary, Business Sponsor
Technical Coordinator, Business Visionary, Business Analyst

spm_questions.spm_question: What role is responsible for ensuring that the solution delivered will enable the benefits described in the Business Case to be achieved?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.2 - The Business Visionary remains involved throughout the project, providing the team with strategic direction and ensuring that the solution delivered will enable the benefits described in the Business Case to be achieved.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which responsibility relates to the Solution Development Team roles?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.2.2.2 -Solution Development Team roles form the ‘engine room’ of the project. They shape and build the solution.

spm_options.spm_option: Ensure that the technical roles work in a consistent way

spm_questions.spm_question: In DSDM, what role must hold a sufficiently high position in the organisation to be able to resolve business issues and make financial decisions?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.1 - This role is the most senior project-level business role. The Business Sponsor is the project champion who is committed to the project, to the proposed solution and the approach to delivering it. The Business Sponsor is specifically responsible for the Business Case and project budget throughout.

spm_questions.spm_question: What DSDM role ensures that the solution/technical roles work in a consistent way?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.3 - As the project’s technical authority, the Technical Coordinator ensures that the solution/technical roles work in a consistent way, that the project is technically coherent and meets the desired technical standards.

spm_questions.spm_question: What DSDM role ensures that the Solution Development Team functions as a whole and meets its objectives?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.6 - The Team Leader ideally acts as the servant-leader for the Solution Development Team and ensures that it functions as a whole and meets its objectives. The Team Leader works with the team to plan and coordinate all aspects of product delivery at the detailed level.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following is a responsibility of the DSDM Project Manager role?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.4 - The Project Manager coordinates all aspects of management of the project at a high level but in line with the DSDM concept of empowerment.

spm_options.spm_option: Creates detailed plans for the actual delivery of the solution
Coordinates all aspects of management of the project at a high level
Leaves all project planning to the Team Leader
Acts as the servant-leader for the Solution Development Team

spm_questions.spm_question: During Iterative Development, which testing activity relates to the role of the Solution Tester?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.3.4.3 - As part of a collaborative team, the Solution Tester will be supporting other roles to fulfill their testing responsibilities by providing testing knowledge and expertise.

spm_questions.spm_question: What role is responsible for providing specific input to the project from the perspective of those who will maintain the solution?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.11 - The Technical Advisor supports the team by providing specific, and often specialist, technical input to the project, often from the perspective of those responsible for operational change management, operational support, ongoing maintenance of the solution, etc.

spm_questions.spm_question: During a Facilitated Workshop, which action relates to the role of the Workshop Facilitator?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.1.3 - Decisions and agreements are not forced. If participants cannot agree on a point, the Workshop Facilitator should recognize this outcome and elicit from the group the appropriate action to remedy the shortfall.

spm_options.spm_option: Ensure their opinion on the content is understood by others
Represent their own interest throughout the workshop
Agree appropriate action with the workshop members to resolve any disagreements
Decide the outcome and document findings

spm_questions.spm_question: Configuration Management in an Agile environment...

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.3.3 - Configuration management is an important consideration as there is sometimes a need to revert to what was previously agreed.

spm_options.spm_option: ..must always be formal and document driven

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is NOT a factor instrumental to Success?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 5.4.1- DSDM requires commitment of business time throughout

spm_options.spm_option: Exclusion of the customer from the lifecycle

spm_questions.spm_question: Which characteristic does NOT relate to the Solution Development Team?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 5.3.2 - Stability is required within the team. A DSDM project will be put at serious risk if team members are swapped in and out.

spm_options.spm_option: Each role empowered to make decisions
Flexibility to swap team members in and out of the team
Desire and authority to make day-to-day decisions

spm_questions.spm_question: What is the purpose of the Feasibility phase?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.3 - The Feasibility phase is intended primarily to establish whether the proposed project is likely to be feasible from a technical perspective and whether it appears cost-effective from a business perspective.

spm_options.spm_option: Converge over time on an accurate solution that meets a business need
Establish whether the project appears costeffective
Establish how development and delivery of the solution will be managed
Bring a baseline of the solution into operational use

test.spm_test_name: The Pre-Project and Foundation Phases and Products

spm_questions.spm_question: To ensure that a DSDM project has appropriate governance applied, it needs to get the balance right between...?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.9 - The DSDM process can be configured for a specific project and the appropriate level of formality can be determined with which the DSDM products are defined and created.

spm_options.spm_option: Too many features and too few features
Too much documentation and too little documentation
Too much formality and too little formality
Too many resources and too few resources

spm_questions.spm_question: What product is the high level definition of the business driver for the project

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.1 - This is an objective of the Terms of Reference

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is not a Business product?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.5 - The Development Approach Definition is a product relating to the solution.

spm_questions.spm_question: The purpose of the delivery plan is to provide a high level schedule of project increments and at least for the first increment, the [?] that make up that increment.

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.6 - The purpose of the delivery plan is to provide a high level schedule of project increments and at least for the first increment, the Timeboxes that make up that increment.

spm_questions.spm_question: When does DSDM state that the PostProject phase takes place?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.7 - After the final Deployment for a project, the PostProject phase checks how well the expected business benefits have been met.

spm_options.spm_option: After the final Deployment for a project

spm_questions.spm_question: What is the purpose of the DSDM PreProject phase?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.2 - The PreProject phase ensures that only the right projects are started, and that they are set up correctly, based on a clearly defined objective.

spm_options.spm_option: Ensures that only the right projects are started and set up correctly
Assesses the viability of the project
Ensures the project can be carried out by the Solution Development Team
Plans and resources the Foundations phase

spm_questions.spm_question: Which objective relates to the DSDM Deployment phase?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.6 - The objective of the Deployment phase is to bring a baseline of the Evolving Solution into operational use. The release that is deployed may be the final solution, or a subset of the final solution. After the last release, the project is formally closed.

spm_options.spm_option: Bring a baseline of the Evolving Solution into operational use
Create a functional solution that demonstrably meets the needs of the business
Give the wider organisation an early view of the solution that they will eventually use
Describe how quality will be assured

spm_questions.spm_question: In the Business Case, what does the business vision describe?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.2 - The business vision describes a changed business as it expected to be, incrementally and at the end of the project.

spm_options.spm_option: Objectives of the project in terms of return on investment
What the changed business is expected to look like
Future projects required to meet business goals

spm_questions.spm_question: Which purpose relates to the Project Approach Questionnaire?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 5.7 - A simple checklist used to assess whether the success factors described above are likely to be met or whether action needs to be taken to counter the risk arising from any of them being undermined.

spm_options.spm_option: Justification for the project from a business perspective
Assess whether the Instrumental Success Factors are likely to be met
List the requirements that the project needs to address and how they meet the business need
Scope and justify the Feasibility phase

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following statements about the Solution Architecture Definition is true? 1. The Solution Architecture Definition contains the strategy for testing and review of the solution. 2. The Solution Architecture Definition contains both business and technical aspects of the solution.

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.4 - The Solution Architecture Definition is intended to cover both business and technical aspects of the solution to a level of detail that makes the scope of the solution clear but does not constrain evolutionary development.

spm_questions.spm_question: What is the Foundation Summary used for?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.9 - A snapshot of the evolving business, solution and management products is captured in the Foundation Summary at the end of the Foundations phase. It is used to help decide as to whether the project is likely to deliver the required return on investment.

spm_options.spm_option: For establishing if the scope of the solution is clear and allows for evolutionary development
To provide a high-level schedule of Project Increments
For helping to decide whether the investment in the project is worthwhile
To prioritise the project within a wider portfolio of projects

test.spm_test_name: Evolutionary Development, Deployment and Post-Project Phases

spm_questions.spm_question: Which product is refined for detail as the projects moves through Evolutionary Development reflecting changes drawn out during timeboxes?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref C3.2 / 8.2.3 - The PRL is baselined at a high level at the end of the Foundations phase and refined for detail as it proceeds through Evolutionary Development.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which DSDM product describes what has been achieved in a Timebox together with any feedback that may influence plans moving forwards?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.12 - The Timebox Review Record captures the feedback from each review that takes place during a Timebox. It describes what has been achieved up to that point together with any feedback that may influence plans moving forwards.

spm_questions.spm_question: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. An organization amenable to incremental delivery of solutions [?] will benefit from early return on investment.

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 5.5 - Each Timebox should ideally deliver a complete potentially deployable increment of the solution, even though there may not be enough at that point to physically deploy it. The sooner a solution is deployed, the sooner a return can be measured.

spm_questions.spm_question: What is the purpose of the Evolutionary Development phase?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.5 - The purpose of the Evolutionary Development phase is to evolve the solution.

spm_options.spm_option: Converge over time on an accurate solution that meets a business need
Establish whether the project appears cost-effective
Establish how development and delivery of the solution will be managed
Bring a baseline of the solution into operational use

spm_questions.spm_question: What are the names of the two styles of Timeboxes?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.2 - DSDM recognizes two styles of Timebox – a DSDM structured Timebox and a free format Timebox.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which of the following elements make up common sense? 1. Sound judgment. 2. Practical judgment. 3. Normal native intelligence. 4. Specialized knowledge

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 3.1 - Common sense sound practical judgment independent of specialized knowledge or training; normal native intelligence.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which role ensures that the solution/technical roles work in a consistent way?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 7.3.3 - The Technical Co-ordinator ensures consistency and that the project is technically coherent.

spm_questions.spm_question: 'A fixed period of time, at the end of which an objective has been met' is a definition of which technique?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.1 - This is the definition of a Timebox the objective of which is usually the completion of one or more deliverables making up a Solution Increment.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is NOT a specific technique defined in the AgilePM approach?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.1 - This is a technique used in the PRINCE2® method not specifically documented in the Agile approach but this does not mean that it can’t be used, where appropriate..

spm_questions.spm_question: The Project Manager attends the Daily Stand-Up...

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 13.2.6 - The Project Manager attends in order to observe progress and pick up escalated issues

spm_questions.spm_question: The Timebox plan is created by the...?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.11 - Created by the Solution Development Team

spm_questions.spm_question: It is recommended that 60% to 80% of Timebox effort should be concentrated on...?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.2.1 - Refinement is where work on the solution is focussed in line with agreed MoSCoW priorities

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is NOT true regarding MoSCoW prioritisation?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.2.1 - A Must Have is guaranteed to be delivered in the overall project; Agile guarantees the Minimum Usable SubseT, which means a Must Have must be delivered

spm_options.spm_option: A Could have that is unsatisfied in an increment may be subsequently demoted to a Wont Have
A Could have that is unsatisfied in an increment may be subsequently promoted to a Must Have for the next increment
A Must have may never be delivered in the overall project
A Must Have for the Project as a whole may not be a Must Have in the first Increment

spm_questions.spm_question: Which is one of the ways that DSDM deals with problems?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 10.2.3 - This is in line with the use of the MoSCoW technique where Could Haves and Should Haves represent contingency.

spm_options.spm_option: Negotiate extra time for the Timebox
Drop the least important feature from the Timebox

spm_questions.spm_question: In a DSDM project, what does the ‘W’ in ‘MoSCoW’ stand for?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 10.1 - MoSCoW is a prioritisation technique for helping to understand and manage priorities. The letters stand for (M)ust Have, (S)hould Have, (C)ould have, (W)on’t Have this time.

spm_questions.spm_question: In a structured Timebox when does the Solution Development Team seek to understand the Timebox objectives and accept them as realistic?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.2.1 - KickOff is a short session for the Solution Development Team to understand the Timebox objectives and accept them as realistic.

spm_questions.spm_question: Under the DSDM MoSCoW rule, which definition describes the Must Have requirement?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 10.2.1 - This is a Must Have as the solution cannot be delivered without it.

spm_options.spm_option: May need some kind of workaround

spm_questions.spm_question: At the Timebox level, what is used to ensure the transparency of process and progress?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 9.4.2 - The combination of a Team Board and the Daily Standup makes visible the necessary elements of control at the level of the Solution Development Team.

spm_questions.spm_question: How long should the Daily Stand-up take?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.3 - Each Daily Stand-up has a short and fixed duration, normally no longer than 15 minutes – two minutes per participant, plus two minutes is a good guide.

spm_options.spm_option: No more than half an hour
Two minutes per participant, plus two minutes

spm_questions.spm_question: What DSDM product identifies Timeboxes for the project?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 8.2.6 - This is a high-level schedule of Project Increments and, at least for the first/imminent Increment, Timeboxes that make up that Increment.

spm_questions.spm_question: ‘To establish whether the product appears cost effective from a business perspective' is an objective of which phase?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 6.3 - This is an objective of the Feasibility phase

spm_questions.spm_question: When using Iterative Development, what should each cycle begin and end with?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.3.1 - In most cases each cycle will start with a thought (consideration of what needs to be done) and finish with a Conversation (to review whether the outcome meets the need and to understand what further work is needed if this is not the case). To achieve this the cycle actually begins and ends with a conversation.

spm_questions.spm_question: When, ideally, is the first instance that a solution should be fully tested and potentially deployable?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 9.3.1 - Ideally the solution will be fully tested at the end of the Timebox, although it is acknowledged that this may not be achievable in all circumstances.

spm_options.spm_option: At the Review stage of Deployment
At the end of a Timebox

spm_questions.spm_question: How often should a Timebox Plan be updated?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 9.2.2 - It is updated at least on a daily basis at the Daily Standups.

spm_questions.spm_question: Which statement about the detail of requirements is correct for DSDM?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 4.6 - DSDM advocates first understanding the scope of the business problem to be solved and the proposed solution, but not in such detail that the project becomes paralysed by overly detailed analysis of requirements.

spm_options.spm_option: Detail emerges sooner rather than later
DSDM teams strive to achieve full detail as early as possible
Detail is expected to emerge over time

spm_questions.spm_question: In a free format Timebox, which activity is done during the Iterative Development step?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 11.2.2 - A free format Timebox is effective where formality and structure is not possible or helpful, but it is still important that reviews are scheduled during the body of free format Timebox.

spm_options.spm_option: Agree what work will be undertaken, agree priorities and accept the workload
Scheduled reviews of the work in progress
Formal acceptance of the Timebox deliverables
Workshop to learn from experience and to take action to improve future Timeboxes

spm_questions.spm_question: What perspectives should be considered when ‘Modelling’?

spm_objectives.spm_reference: [] AgilePM ref 12.2.2 - A coherent picture of a solution area can be gained by considering the perspectives of: what, where, when, how, who and why, and the relationship between them.

spm_options.spm_option: How many, how often and at what cost
What, where, when, how, who and why
